_what: What a Waiting on you row's done_when_rule (src/lists.json kind done-when-rule) can be checked over (src/done-when.mjs): each source id is a real current read of the thing it names, shaped into rows with typed fields the formula engine's rules compare. `reader` names the read the owner (src/person-store.mjs doneWhenReaders) answers fresh every time, an array of items (or { items, fields } when the fields are only known at the read: `flat` rows are used as they come, `spread` copies the item's object at that path in as extra fields of the kind named). `row` says how each field is read from an item: a path list (the first path holding a value wins), { value }, or { path, as: boolean | ms | number, equals?, default? }. `named_by` is a field whose is_text / is_any_of tests in the rule name the things to look at (a file's path, a job's id), so the reader looks only at those. `prefix` makes the id a family (list:<list id>), the rest of the id handed to the reader as its `arg`; `fields_reader` answers that family's fields without reading rows. `noun` is how the source's rows are called in a refusal. `newest` bounds how many of the newest items of each named thing a reader looks at (arrived: what a carrier route brought, the person's own words in that place, read from the message speaker index, so a download is checked by its kind in the words the carrier wrote, such as a route of Downloads and text containing .cer, never by an exact file name). Nothing here is cached: a source is read each time a row is checked. `rows_most` bounds how many records a check will load (more fails with too_many, naming the count). `columns` (saved-logins) maps each field to the one plain SQL column holding it, so a check reads only the columns its rule names, never the sealed values.

matches.what: at least one row passes the rule

computer-sources.label: What the person's computers can read

list.label: Rows of one of the person's lists (list:<list id>)

arrived.label: What the person's own places brought, by route (a Mac's Downloads or Screenshots, Voice Memos, any carrier), newest first

work.label: Work handed to AIs and things given to the person, by id

words.no_rule: Trillion can't check this by itself. Press Done when it's done.
words.device: Waiting for one of your devices to show it's done.
words.unfinished: Trillion can't check this by itself: its check is not finished ({why}). Press Done when it's done.
words.unknown_source: Trillion can't check this by itself: it has no way to look at {over}. Press Done when it's done.
words.failed: Couldn't check just now: {reason}. Trying again in {seconds} s.
words.row_done: already done: it was marked Done
words.no_longer_held: no longer waiting: it is not waiting on you any more
words.row_gone: no longer waiting: it is not on the list
words.bad_over: done_when_rule.over "{over}" is not something Trillion can check. It can check: {allowed}.
words.bad_list: done_when_rule.over "{over}" names a list this person does not keep. list_lists shows their lists.
words.bad_says: done_when_rule.says is the plain words of what is counted, read after "<passing> of <all> ", such as "logins your AIs can read"; it must be 1 to {chars} characters.
words.bad_tree: done_when_rule.tree must be a rule group { kind: "group", combinator: "and" | "or", negate: false, rules: [{ kind: "rule", field, operator, params }] } with at least one rule and at most {most}.
words.bad_field: done_when_rule.tree names the field "{field}", which {over} does not have. Its fields are: {fields}.
words.bad_operator: done_when_rule.tree uses the operator "{operator}", which is not one of the operators for {field} ({kind}). Allowed: {allowed}.
words.bad_params: done_when_rule.tree: the rule on {field} ({operator}) is missing what it compares with ({input}).
words.needs_names: done_when_rule.tree must name what to look at with {field} is_text (or is_any_of), because {over} looks only at the {noun} named.
